references.text: Cain kills his brother Abel – an early example of sibling rivalry and deadly conflict that can be compared to Esau's hatred and murder plans against Jacob.
Jacob prepares to meet Esau again and fears for his life because of Esau's hatred and previous threat to kill him.
Esau runs toward Jacob and embraces him, showing reconciliation after the long conflict that began with the blessing.
The Lord declares His love for Jacob and His hatred for Esau, reflecting the deep opposition between the two brothers.
Warning against godlessness like Esau, who sold his birthright and later found no opportunity for repentance even though he sought the blessing with tears.
Obadiah prophesies that Esau (Edom) will be put to shame for violence against his brother Jacob – a long-standing conflict that began with the hatred in Gen 27:41.
Chronological precursor: The verse shows the moment when Esau learns about the blessing, which directly triggers the hatred and murder threat in the source verse.
Theological contrast: Human hatred between brothers (Esau) is set against God's eternal choice of Jacob.
Escalation of conflict: From bitter crying over the loss (v.34) to planned murder (v.41).
Cause and effect: The deception in this verse is the direct cause of the hatred and murder threat in the source verse.
Consequence and solution: Jacob's fear of Esau's revenge (v.41) leads to the strategy of reconciliation in this verse.
Theological comment: Paul uses the Esau/Jacob relationship (as described in the source verse) to illustrate God's sovereign choice.
